findings.text: the assertion `exit_record.get("worker_pid") == worker_pid` is vacuous — the wait at :810-816 returns a record only when it already carries that pid — so it states a property the wait enforces and would not redden on any change that leaves the wait in place.

the worker-record payload is composed at two sites in one module — the new writer here and the post-watch block at :3835-3853 — so the two can drift in field set, and the later write immediately overwrites the early one; one helper should serve both.

the after arm's log ends `run 10 EXIT=0 8s` instead of the bare `EXIT=<code>` line the record contract names as where promotion reads a gate's status, so the head arm's receipt rests on the manifest's exit_status rather than on the log.

with the repair reverted this case reddens only intermittently (the worker's own measurement: one failure in five at a fixture-repaired base), so it is a weak regression guard however green the ten head runs are; the thirty-second stub sleep against a thirty-second startup watch leaves the race undecided.
